Use Tier 2: replace MultVAE’s all-item reconstruction objective with masked-item denoising, retaining the residual architecture and SASRec ensemble. The 16-negative SASRec experiment reduced macro validation HR@10 from 0.6250 to 0.6162, so start from the supplied 0.6250 implementation with one-negative BCE. The hypothesis is that reconstructing visible items lets the residual VAE learn an identity shortcut; predicting withheld training items should strengthen its ability to recommend unseen items.

Modify data_processing_and_feature_engineering and model_design together: for each binary training history containing at least two items, randomly withhold approximately half its items, ensuring both context and targets are nonempty. Encode only the retained items using the existing normalized EmbeddingBag and residual pathway, and compute multinomial reconstruction loss only on withheld items. Replace the existing input dropout with this explicit masking, preserve KL annealing, and retain ordinary reconstruction for singleton histories. Draw masks solely from training histories using the seed-42 training stream; keep supplied splits, catalog definitions, all four datasets, and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] unchanged.

In training_evaluation, preserve architecture dimensions, optimizer settings, training limits, checkpoint selection, and equal-weight mean-rank fusion so this experiment isolates the denoising objective. Validation and exported inference must both encode the complete available history without masking and produce scores through the trained models; preserve dataset routing and verify checkpoint reload and predictor parity. Report actual per-category member and ensemble metrics and macro validation HR@10 against 0.6250, print Final Validation Score, and respect the remaining shared GPU budget; leave hidden-test access and final prediction generation to the host evaluator.
